Back-transform predictor variables from a logit model

Source: R/internal_functions.R
unlogit.Rd

Returns the predictor value at which a binomial logit model reaches probability p (e.g. L50 for p = 0.5) with a 95% delta-method confidence interval.

Usage

unlogit(p, model)

Arguments

p

probability threshold to unlog from model

model

a glm model object with a single predictor

Value

A data frame with columns mean, ci.min and ci.max

Details

The estimate is \(x_p = (logit(p) - b_0) / b_1\). Its variance is approximated by the delta method, \(Var(x_p) = g^T V g\), where \(V\) is the variance-covariance matrix of the intercept and slope (vcov(model)) and \(g = (-1/b_1, -x_p/b_1)\) is the gradient of \(x_p\). The confidence interval is \(x_p \pm z_{0.975} SE\). This accounts for the (typically strong negative) correlation between intercept and slope and is equivalent to MASS::dose.p().
